long_biography.plain_text:
Daughter of industrialist Suhail Bahwan, she studied computer science and entered business through information technology. At 23 she launched a venture with S. Durgaprasad, taking an outward-looking approach from its 1999 formation. Bahwan CyberTek moved beyond services toward proprietary products, predictive analytics and industry systems, giving its founder a distinct entrepreneurial record inside a powerful family context.

That operating base supported a broader portfolio and an increasingly public governance role. Bahwan now oversees interests that include clean power, hydrogen projects, specialist education and trading, while retaining strategic responsibility for the original company. As chair of the Family Business Council Gulf, she also works on succession and resilience among regional family enterprises.
